reviews.comment: Taught very clearly, but posts no material online and requires all notes taken in class. Shows a love for the subject and is eager to explain topics more in depth if needed.
Great professor who clearly loves what he teaches. Every test was curved by 20 points. If you do the bare minimum by going to class and just write stuff down you will easily get an A. Really cool guy
reviews.ratingTags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While the professor is extremely passionate about what he is teaching, his whole lecture is him telling stories about his experiences. There is no textbook and slides are not posted.The grades are only 3 exams and 2 assignments (that the university made him add) Exams are 90% of your grade and include a handwritten essay section.2 essays each exam.
reviews.ratingTags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Go to class! He does not post his slides and the grades are only tests. He is a sweet professor who knows a lot about the subject, but the class structure could have been a lot better. There are only 3 grades and they are tests, so make sure you take good notes!

GO TO CLASS! If you go to class, you will do well on exams! It is challenging but as long as you put in the work, you'll be alright. He's very caring and clearly passionate about the lectures he gives. He doesn't post slides, but lets you take pictures of them. Taking notes is important! He's happy to answer questions. Overall a great professor.

You do not have to show up to class, but he does not post his slides. Just take note of everything on the slides and start studying for the exams early. It is a lot of information, but once you take the first test, you know what to study and look for. He is a really sweet professor and helped me whenever I had questions.

I took this course as my language, philosophy, and culture credit, and I wish I could go back in time. I would've Q dropped but I need the full-time hours. He does not review, have a textbook or post slides. I walked into all 3 exams blindly. I studied relentlessly for 2 weeks before the second exam and still only got an 85 with the curve.

Dr. Pulak is a good professor. He's available when you need him and understanding. There is no textbook so attend class! There are only 3 grades in the course in the form of three exams, but he does curve them based on class averages. Put in the work and show up to class and you'll be fine. Not a cakewalk, but also not very difficult.

While this was the hardest class of my semester, it was the most interesting.  Dr. Pulak is so knowledgeable and  passionate about what he teaches, it is impossible not to be enthralled.  There is no homework, but a lot of studying is necessary if you want a hope in heck of doing well on the exams!  You must go to class if you want to pass!

Dr. Pulak is very knowledgeable about Nautical Archaeology, he played a part in the excavation of several shipwrecks covered. Every exam question comes from the slideshow he lectures from, not from his anecdotes. He gave a very generous curve on each exam. It was an interesting elective that gives you some fun facts about ancient shipbuilding
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS
